newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE RETURNS WITH SOMETHING TO PROVE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE RETURNS WITH SOMETHING TO PROVE.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie returns to the European Tour on Thursday for the first time since a disappointing U.S. Masters last month on a course he stormed away from a year ago.

Montgomerie had good reason then to complain at last year's Benson and Hedges International at the Oxfordshire Club when foul weather frustrated many of the Tour's top golfers and the burly Scotsman strode from the final hole in a rage after a closing round of 84.
He is still comfortably leading the Ryder Cup standings, the overriding target for leading players this season, but will still be desperately keen for a good finish.
Montgomerie, Europe's top player for the past four years and ranked six in the world, will be up against a Tour veteran who produced a stunning performance last weekend to win the Italian Open.
Bernhard Langer carded a final round course-record 64 to overhaul a three-stroke lead by Jose Maria Olazabal with a storming finish of four birdies in the last five holes.

It signalled an extraordinary renaissance for Langer who has resorted to the long-handled putter after periodic attacks of the 'yips' on the greens and had not won a European tournament for nearly two years.

That victory also raised Langer from 20th to 16th place in the world rankings, keeping intact his feat of being one of only two golfers to have been in the top 20 since rankings began in 1986. The other is Greg Norman, the world number one.
The Italian Open also continued Olazabal's remarkable return after 18 months out of the sport because of an agonising foot condition.
In seven tournaments since his return, he has yet to finish lower than 12th and has already fought his way up to 10th in the Ryder Cup standings.
But Olazabal will be missing from the field at this Oxfordshire course as he is restricting himself to not playing more than two tournaments in succession.
The success last weekend could act as a spur for another veteran, Ian Woosnam, who has so far been largely unsuccessful on this year's Tour, although he is still ninth in the Ryder Cup rankings.
The Welshman should have won the early season Desert Classic in Dubai but a fluffed chip into the water at the final hole of the closing round saw him lose out to Australian Richard Green.
Ryder Cup captain Severiano Ballesteros will be hoping for solid performances by each of his veterans to ensure their automatic selection for the biennial challenge.
Ballesteros will also be teeing off on Thursday but only an optimist will bet on his name appearing on the leader board. So far this season he has made the cut only once.
